_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

notes: A personal token is the simpler path for one workspace and is what Flux offers first; OAuth is for connecting more than one account or for a build shared with other people.
The token endpoint returns form-encoded by default; send Accept: application/json to get JSON back.

repo is all-or-nothing and includes private repositories and write access - GitHub has no read-only repo scope for OAuth apps. If that is too broad, a GitHub App with fine-grained permissions is the right shape instead, and that is a different registration.
The device flow is available and is the better fit for a desktop browser than a loopback redirect.

personal_token.label: Fine-grained personal access token
personal_token.where: github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens - pick the repositories and grant Contents, Issues and Pull requests as read-only unless a task needs to write.
notes: A fine-grained token is strictly better than the OAuth repo scope here: repo is all-or-nothing across every repository you can see, and fine-grained is per repository and per permission.

create_issue_comment.notes: A comment notifies subscribers, so it is outbound.

rate_limits.note: Search is separately limited to 30 requests per minute. Both return the remaining budget in x-ratelimit-remaining; read it rather than counting.

notes: github.com returns 403 through this container's egress proxy, so the endpoints could not be probed directly.
